old_caption: The video captures a serene seascape under a partly cloudy sky. The ocean stretches out to the horizon, its surface shimmering with the reflection of sunlight. The water is a deep blue, with gentle waves rippling across it, creating a dynamic yet peaceful scene. The clouds above are fluffy and white, scattered across the sky, allowing patches of blue to peek through. The sun's rays filter through these gaps, casting a bright, sparkling light on the water below. There are no visible animals or characters in the frame, emphasizing the untouched beauty of nature. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the vast expanse of the sea and the sky, providing a tranquil and immersive view of the natural world.

caption: The video captures a wide, open-ocean view beneath a bright, partly cloudy sky. A flat horizon line sits near the vertical middle, separating deep blue water below from pale blue sky filled with scattered cumulus clouds above. Sunlight produces a broad, glittering band of specular reflection on the water surface, brightest just below the horizon and fading toward the foreground, where small dark wave crests and ripples are visible. The sea surface continuously undulates, with foreground crests and ripples shifting position and shape. The glittering reflection band flickers and reorganizes its sparkle pattern as the waves move, while its overall location and extent remain stable. The framing is essentially constant, and no object enters or leaves the scene. The horizon, cloud arrangement, and reflective band persist across the visible portion.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless

camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
